AFWD.chosen_element: construction of the SIXTEEN_3 trilattice geometry

AREV.justification: a reverse transformation that verifies the derived coupling field remains invariant when traced back to the vacuum, confirming the derivation is reversible

CLINK.justification: sequential chaining that links the reconstituted coupling field to a projective measurement that extracts the numerical value of α

ENGAGR.chosen_element: dialetheic coupling branch (both true and false simultaneously)
ENGAGR.justification: the I‑arm of the SIXTEEN_3 lattice, holding the paradox that the vacuum fluctuates between coupled and decoupled states, essential for the measured value of α

EVALF.justification: the false evaluator arm where the magnetic component alone would give a vanishing coupling

EVALT.justification: the true evaluator arm where the electric component of the vacuum yields a non‑zero fine‑structure constant

FFUSE.chosen_element: multiplication that recombines the three arms
FFUSE.justification: reconstitutes exactly the coupling potential that entered the split; the identity coupling field is recovered, guaranteeing FFUSE(FSPLIT(x)) = x

FSPLIT.chosen_element: tri‑ary branching of the electromagnetic coupling potential
FSPLIT.justification: co‑multiplication that fans the single coupling field into three evaluator arms: electric (true), magnetic (false), and dialetheic (both)

IFIX.chosen_element: permanent append‑only record of the derived constant
IFIX.justification: irreversible fixation that etches the obtained fine‑structure constant into the axiomatic store, making it an immutable fact of the system

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: self‑reference of the trilattice at the pinch
IMSCRIB.justification: the identity element where the whole lattice recognises itself as a structure capable of hosting the coupling, without yet splitting

TANCH.chosen_element: the closed boundary of the derivation
TANCH.justification: the final step that seals the entire derivation, ensuring the obtained fine‑structure constant is contained within the axiomatic system

VINIT.justification: no lattice, no coupling, no constant; the absolute void before any SIXTEEN_3 configuration is instantiated

steps.domain_action: the derivation begins from an unstructured quantum vacuum, devoid of any lattice or coupling
the SIXTEEN_3 trilattice geometry is constructed – the (1,1) horn torus, the FSPLIT3 sphere, and the three evaluator stations are instantiated
the trilattice self‑identifies at the pinch point, recognising itself as the carrier of the coupling potential
the single electromagnetic coupling potential is branched into three evaluator arms – the electric arm (T), the magnetic arm (F), and the dialetheic arm (I)
on the true arm the coupling is evaluated and found non‑zero, corresponding to a finite fine‑structure constant
on the false arm the coupling is evaluated as zero, representing a decoupled electromagnetic vacuum
the dialetheic arm holds both true and false simultaneously, capturing the quantum‑fluctuation paradox that underlies the observed constant
multiplication recombines the three arms, reconstituting exactly the coupling potential that was originally split
a contravariant descent back towards the vacuum verifies that the recovered coupling field is invariant under reversal
the reconstituted coupling is composed with a projective measurement operation that extracts the numerical value of the fine‑structure constant
the derived constant α is irreversibly recorded in the axiomatic store, becoming a permanent truth of the system
the derivation is sealed – the whole sequence from vacuum to recorded α forms a closed boundary
